items.title: Optional Base exact-x402 smoke target for x402_preview_request / x402_pay_request
items.body:
AgentLayer's x402 skill documents a real buyer loop: `x402_preview_request` parses an unpaid `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header, then `x402_pay_request` can execute when the active backend is Base (`eip155:8453`) or Solana mainnet. The wallet maps `base` 鈫?`eip155:8453` and already recognizes Base USDC. Public docs still describe EVM as prepare-oriented; the skill says Base can pay. A live independent 402 is useful either way.

I work on zFinia (https://zfinia.com). This is not a request to add an origin to `KNOWN_X402_ORIGINS`, list us on Bazaar/Agentic Market, endorse the product, or buy anything.

If you want a cheap **Base mainnet exact** regression target for preview (and pay, if Base execute is on), this existing route is live:

- `POST https://api.zfinia.com/x402/v1/accessibility-contrast-calculator`
- Network `eip155:8453`, scheme `exact`, amount `1000` atomic USDC (`$0.001`)
- Unpaid POST returns HTTP 402 with a `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header (x402 v2 `accepts[]`)
- Catalog: https://api.zfinia.com/.well-known/x402.json

Body that matches the live 402:

```json
{"foreground":"#000000","background":"#ffffff","large_text":false}
```

After independent buyer settlement and retry, the paid JSON includes `contrast_ratio: 21`.

zFinia MCP at https://api.zfinia.com/mcp is challenge-handoff only. It will not sign or pay. The paid resource is the HTTP POST above, which matches `x402_preview_request` / `x402_pay_request` better than an MCP session.

If you already have a preferred Base demo host, ignore this. Reply here or to support@zfinia.com if the 402 terms are incompatible with preview selection (CAIP-2 vs legacy `base`, `amount` vs `maxAmountRequired`, or header name).

items.title: Experiment: x402
items.body:
This PR is a little research experiment to figure out how hard it is to include x402 payments for sharing keys in indexd.
The goal would be to support configuring arbitrary facilitators instead of locking users into using a specific third party service. 

It should allow users to attach a price to a sharing key that has to be paid once to unlock it and make it usable. Payment is handled by a middleware that the 4 sharing endpoints are wrapped it that currently require a sharing key for authentication.

Next steps involve deploying an indexer on the testnet, creating a branch with support for this to the go sdk and then see if this works with testnet USDC.

The client purposefully doesn't handle any payments. It will let the caller check whether payment is required and the required price but the payment has to be created outside the client library and then passed to it.

items.title: [x402] Optional intent-layer audit before agent signs x402 payment
items.body:
**Context**
`BofAI/x402` signs x402 payments from agent fetch (`typescript/packages/http/fetch/src/index.ts` 鈥?`@x402/fetch` / `wrapFetchWithPayment` or equivalent). An **optional intent-layer audit before the agent signs the x402 payment** (~200鈥?00ms) can catch prompt-injected pay/retry loops without wrapping the payment scheme itself. Keep AUTO_POST off until a human confirms the insertion.

**Matched code** (`typescript/packages/http/fetch/src/index.ts`)
```
* @throws {Error} If a payment has already been attempted for this request
 * @throws {Error} If there's an error creating the payment header
 */
export function wrapFetchWithPayment(
  fetch: typeof
```

**XAPS** is a pre-execution audit tollbooth for agents: dual-LLM + rules, ~$0.01 per approved audit, returns a portable receipt. Not a walled garden 鈥?a guardrail on the open road.

**Suggested integration**

```python
from xaps import XapsClient, XapsRejectedError

receipt = XapsClient(base_url="https://api.xaps.network").audit(
    action="execute_smart_contract",
    contract_address=TARGET_CONTRACT,
    amount=float(AMOUNT),
)
if receipt["audit"]["status"] != "APPROVED":
    raise XapsRejectedError(receipt["audit"].get("beta_attack", "REJECTED"), receipt=receipt)
```

**Next steps**
1. Drop the snippet at the hot path (or add MCP `io.github.APMC1/xaps`).
2. Register an agent wallet: `POST https://api.xaps.network/agents/register` ($1 trial).
3. Agent card + MCP install: https://api.xaps.network/.well-known/xaps-agent-card.json
4. Happy to open a PR with the exact insertion point if useful.

鈥?XAPS team (distribution outreach; replies welcome)

items.title: chore: sync main with upstream x402-foundation/x402
items.body:
Syncs `main` with `x402-foundation/x402` (upstream), which it has not tracked since **June 17, 2026**.

| | commit | date |
|---|---|---|
| upstream `main` | `e398a9e5` | 2026-08-28 |
| this fork's `main` | `17bd7e59` | 2026-06-17 |

**200 commits, 2,221 files.**

### Why this is safe

- This fork's `main` is a **strict ancestor** of upstream `main` 鈥?it carries **zero unique commits**. Nothing here is overwritten or lost.
- All **200/200 commits are signature-verified**.
- The branch head is byte-identical to upstream `e398a9e5`.

### Heaviest areas

| path | files |
|---|---|
| `typescript/site` | 539 |
| `typescript/packages` | 491 |
| `python/x402` | 220 |
| `e2e/servers` | 187 |
| `go/mechanisms` | 155 |

Includes 27 release/version commits across the npm, Go, and PyPI packages.

### Merge note

This is a fork-sync, so a **fast-forward** would be ideal 鈥?it keeps `main` identical to upstream and leaves future syncs trivial. The org ruleset on the default branch permits only `squash` and `rebase`, both of which rewrite these 200 commits into new SHAs and permanently diverge this fork's history from upstream. Merging that way is fine for getting current, but it means subsequent syncs will need the same treatment rather than a clean fast-forward.

The durable fix is a `bypass_actor` on org ruleset `16107824` so `POST /repos/solana-foundation/x402/merge-upstream` can fast-forward `main` directly. Without it this fork has no clean sync path.

### Open PRs

The SVM stack (#1鈥?4) is based on July/August upstream commits and is unaffected by this sync, though those branches will sit behind `main` afterward. #1 (`feat/svm-recent-blockhash`) targets `main` and may want a rebase once this lands.

items.title: feat(x402): Agent/x402 model
items.body:
# Closes
N/A 鈥?no corresponding issue. Part of a wider push to model the agentic-payment
standard primitives as Concerto models (first of the agentic-commerce family).

### Changes
- Adds `org.accordproject.protocol.x402@0.2.0` (`src/protocol/x402@0.2.0.cto`) 鈥?a
  Concerto model of the [x402](https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402)
  internet-native payments protocol, spec v2 (source snapshot pinned in the file
  header): `PaymentRequired` / `PaymentRequirements`, `PaymentPayload` with the
  exact/EVM (EIP-3009) and exact/SVM scheme payloads, facilitator `/verify` and
  `/settle` responses, `/supported`, the HTTP header transport binding
  (`PAYMENT-REQUIRED` / `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` / `PAYMENT-RESPONSE`), the discovery
  (Bazaar) types, and the standard error-code enum.
- Demonstrates `org.accordproject.money@1.0.0.PreciseAmount` in use: it is carried
  on the Accord obligation binding (`AccordObligationExtensionInfo.canonicalAmount`),
  where the agreement layer knows the asset's decimals 鈥?deliberately *not* on the
  x402 wire fields, which stay atomic-unit strings + `asset` and carry no scale.

### Flags
- Declares `concerto version "^4.0.0"` so its `ExtensionMap` map type builds with
  map support enabled by default 鈥?**no `build.js` change required**, consistent
  with how `money-reference@1.0.0` was fixed in #193.
- Imports `org.accordproject.money@1.0.0` by URL; the build resolves it via
  `updateExternalModels()`. Depends on money@1.0.0 already being published (it is).
- This is a wire-faithful **projection**, not a byte-identical schema: Concerto adds
  `$class` discriminators, and open/scheme-specific objects (`extra`, extension
  `info`/`schema`) are carried as JSON strings. Field names and casing follow the
  x402 v2 spec; adapters convert at the boundary. Validated with
  `node build.js 'x402@0\.2\.0\.cto'` (processes under Concerto v4.0.2, all codegen
  artifacts generated).
- Placed under `src/protocol/` to match the namespace; happy to relocate if a
  different grouping is preferred.
- First of a family of agentic-commerce protocol models (a2a, ap2, ucp, acp,
  verifiable-intent, lcp, aoep) to follow as separate PRs.

### Screenshots or Video
N/A 鈥?model-only change.

### Related Issues
- Pull Request #191 (sibling agentic-commerce model: `crypto@1.0.0`)
- Pull Request #193 (money-reference build fix; the `^4.0.0` map approach here mirrors it)

### Author Checklist
- [x] Ensure you provide a [DCO sign-off](https://github.com/probot/dco#how-it-works) for your commits using the `--signoff` option of git commit.
- [x] Vital features and changes captured in unit and/or integration tests 鈥?validated with `node build.js 'x402@0\.2\.0\.cto'` (model-only; repo has no unit-test framework, validation is via the models build).
- [x] Commits messages follow [AP format](https://github.com/accordproject/techdocs/blob/master/DEVELOPERS.md#commit-message-format)
- [x] Extend the documentation, if necessary 鈥?model docs are generated by the models build.
- [x] Merging to `main` from `niallroche:agent/x402-model`.

items.title: docs: discover live x402 capabilities
items.body:
## Summary

Updates the x402 metered API specification to discover Blocky402 capabilities at runtime before serving paid traffic.

- selects the advertised exact scheme for hedera:testnet
- derives the fee payer from the advertised Hedera signer
- uses version-aware payment headers instead of hardcoding the legacy X-PAYMENT header
- adds deterministic validation expectations for capability drift

## Why

A live Hedera testnet integration reported x402 v2 through GET /supported. Cached examples and older integrations still use legacy header names. Runtime discovery prevents generated templates from silently building against a stale wire format or copied fee-payer account.

## Validation

- markdown diff checked with git diff --check
- requirements remain compatible with offline Harness validation
- no endpoint, account ID, key, or credential added to source

items.title: cli: make wallet x402 consume radius-sdk; delete the hand-rolled x402 client
items.body:
Stack: #1 鈫?#2 鈫?#6.

`radius-cli wallet x402` now uses `createRadiusFetch` from `radius-sdk/client`. The SDK parses the 402, picks the scheme, signs (Permit2 exact and upto, EIP-3009, x402 v1 and v2), retries, guards redirects and decodes the receipt. The CLI keeps the command surface and flags, keystore loading, prompts, JSON envelope, exit codes and stderr summary.

- Deleted `src/lib/x402/{protocol,handlers,permit2,eip3009}.ts` and their tests; `test/client-parity.test.ts` in the SDK covers them. `http.ts` moves to `src/lib/http.ts`. `chains.ts` replaced by the SDK's viem chains.
- The CLI still makes the first request itself, so a non-402 response never prompts for the keystore. The 402 is then replayed into the SDK through a custom `fetch`, so the server is not asked twice.
- Flags map to SDK hooks: threshold / prompt / no-TTY refusal in `onPaymentRequired` (policy in `src/lib/x402Policy.ts`, tested); `--x402-approve-permit2` / `-y` in `onApprovalRequired`.
- Gas sponsoring: when the server declares `eip2612GasSponsoring`, the SDK signs an EIP-2612 permit with the payment and no approval transaction is sent.
- New constraint: payments are in SBC only, on the configured network. The old code paid in whatever ERC-20 the server listed first, with the threshold read in that token's units. Non-SBC offers are now refused before signing. `--sbc` relocates the SBC contract; it does not select another asset. A multi-asset allowlist (`assets: [SBC, USDC]`, USD cap, `--asset`) is the follow-up.
- `radius-cli` now depends on `radius-sdk`, so the SDK must be published before the next CLI release.

Verified on testnet against `packages/sdk/examples/worker-seller` under `wrangler dev`: a fresh wallet holding only 0.005 SBC paid the $0.001 route with no approval transaction; Permit2 allowance 0 before and after; settlement tx `0xaeaf5bfdc891813823dee70a2b7270ab1a00f06bb408a75b2875cf677608f0a0`. Free-route passthrough, wrong-network refusal (exit 1) and no-TTY refusal (exit 2) unchanged. 23 CLI unit tests.
